gloss: to catch the eye; to attract attention

definitions.gloss: to catch the eye; to stand out; to draw attention
definitions.explanation: Said of something whose appearance makes people look at it — a bright color, an unusual design, a striking headline. The thing that stands out is the subject; the person who notices takes の or は when mentioned at all.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{看板|かんばん}が{目|め}を{引|ひ}く。
examples.english: The red sign catches your eye.

examples.japanese: {会場|かいじょう}で{一番|いちばん}{目|め}を{引|ひ}いたのは{彼女|かのじょ}の{作品|さくひん}だった。
examples.english: The piece that stood out most at the venue was hers.

examples.japanese: {棚|たな}に{並|なら}んだ{商品|しょうひん}の{中|なか}で、そのパッケージだけが{客|きゃく}の{目|め}を{引|ひ}いていた。
examples.english: Among all the products on the shelf, only that package was catching customers' eyes.

notes:
USAGE:
Common in advertising and design talk: a display, headline, or outfit {目|め}を{引|ひ}く when it succeeds in standing out. The judgment is neutral to positive; drawing unwanted stares is {目立|めだ}つ or {人目|ひとめ}を{引|ひ}く instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}の{目|め}を{引|ひ}く: to catch people's attention
- {目|め}を{引|ひ}くデザイン: an eye-catching design
- {一際|ひときわ}{目|め}を{引|ひ}く: to stand out conspicuously

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {目立|めだ}つ: to be conspicuous — a state, with no implication that anyone is drawn in
- {目|め}を{奪|うば}う: to be captivating — much stronger, holding the viewer's gaze

cross_references.label: to catch one's eye, to stand out
